title: The Book of Common Prayer (1662 text): A Catechism (with the Ten Commandments and 'my duty towards my Neighbour') and The Form of Solemnization of Matrimony
author: Church of England
date_of_work: 1662 (text as printed in the 1693 London edition)
source_url: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/textcreationpartnership/A28758/master/A28758.xml (EEBO-TCP A28758; The Book of Common Prayer ... according to the use of the Church of England, London: Charles Bill and the executrix of Thomas Newcomb, 1693)
license: CC0 1.0 (EEBO-TCP keyed text); underlying work public domain in the US (note: in the UK the 1662 Prayer Book text remains subject to Crown prerogative/letters patent for printing)
notes: Two offices complete, from a 1693 printing of the 1662 Book (no 1662 printing is available in EEBO-TCP; the authorised text did not change between 1662 and 1693). # = office title. Catechism speaker labels merged into the following line as **Question.** / **Answer.** ¶ = rubric. The fifth commandment and the duty 'to love, honour, and succour my father and mother' are in the Catechism; the marriage service includes the giving away of the bride, the vows ('to love, cherish, and to obey') and the closing exhortation on the duties of husbands and wives.

title: A Perambulation of Kent: 'The Customes of Kent' (Lambarde's discourse on gavelkind: partible descent among all sons, the half for the widow and for the widower, wardship by the next of blood, alienation at fifteen, 'the father to the boughe, and the son to the plough') and the Custumal of Kent with his interlinear English
author: William Lambarde
license: CC0 1.0 (EEBO-TCP Phase II keyed text); underlying work public domain
notes: Two parts: (1) Lambarde's chapter 'The Customes of Kent', complete; (2) the Custumal of Kent (Consuetudines Kanciae) as printed by Lambarde with an English word-by-word gloss above the Anglo-Norman text: rendered here as 'English:' (the gloss read continuously) followed by 'French:' (the original). Margin notes inline as [margin: ...]. [p. N] = page of the 1576 edition. Original spelling (u/v, i/j, macrons) kept. Used in place of Robinson's Common Law of Kent (1741), whose archive.org OCR (1822 and 1858 editions) was too noisy to ship cleanly.

license: Public domain (1898 text). The Liberty Fund 2010 reprint's added bibliography by S. F. C. Milsom (copyright) is excluded.

title: An Act for the Relief of the Poor (Poor Relief Act 1601), 43 Eliz. I c. 2
author: Parliament of England
source_url: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/aep/Eliz1/43/2/enacted (page images: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/aep/Eliz1/43/2/pdfs/aep_16010002_en.pdf, a reprint by Eyre and Spottiswoode, Queen's Printers, 1892)
license: Public domain (1601 statute; 1892 reprint); legislation.gov.uk material under the Open Government Licence v3.0
notes: Complete Act, sections I-XX as numbered in this edition (the first section is unnumbered in the print and is labelled [I.] here). Text produced by OCR (tesseract) of the legislation.gov.uk page images and corrected by hand against the images; marginal side-notes, running heads and signatures omitted; modernised spelling and capitalisation are those of the 1892 reprint, not of the 1601 sessional print. Key sections: I (overseers; setting children and the idle to work; relief of the lame, impotent, old and blind; apprenticing poor children), IV (apprenticeship to 24/21 or marriage), V (cottages on the waste), VII (father, grandfather, mother, grandmother and children of the impotent poor to relieve them at their own charges, as Quarter Sessions assess, on pain of 20s a month). Section numbering differs in other editions (some number the relatives' clause s. 6 or s. 7).

title: An Act for the better Releife of the Poore of this Kingdom (Poor Relief Act 1662; the 'Settlement Act'), 13 & 14 Car. II c. 12
author: Parliament of England
source_url: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/aep/Cha2/14/12/enacted (enacted text as printed in Statutes of the Realm, vol. 5)
license: Public domain (1662 statute); legislation.gov.uk text under the Open Government Licence v3.0
notes: Complete Act, sections I-XXV. Original spelling as in Statutes of the Realm (editorial brackets such as discouragem[en]t kept). '[side-note: ...]' = the section titles supplied by legislation.gov.uk; '[margin: ...]' = marginal notes carried in the enacted-text XML. Key family/settlement provisions: s. I (removal within forty days, on complaint of churchwardens or overseers, of newcomers renting under 10 pounds a year who are likely to be chargeable, to the parish of last legal settlement as native, householder, sojourner, apprentice or servant for forty days), II (appeal to Quarter Sessions), III (harvest workers with certificates), XIX (seizure of goods and rents of putative fathers and mothers who run away and leave bastard children on the parish).
